item.title: Hela to welcome National Fire Service, establish permanent base in Tari
item.description: The Hela Provincial Government will today officially welcome the National Fire Service and invite them to establish a permanent presence in Hela Province, says Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu. Angu said this is a key initiative by HPG, under the leadership of governor Philip Undialu, to strengthen fire, emergency and public safety services across the province.
item.content:encoded:
The Hela Provincial Government will today officially welcome the National Fire Service and invite them to establish a permanent presence in Hela Province, says Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu.

Angu said this is a key initiative by HPG, under the leadership of governor Philip Undialu, to strengthen fire, emergency and public safety services across the province.

The official program will begin promptly at 1pm today. The National Fire Service delegation will return to Port Moresby tomorrow.

Expected to attend are governor Undialu, PNG Chief Fire Officer Bill Roo, senior fire service officers and other invited guests.

“All public servants are requested to assemble at the Hela Education Office for the official program,” Angu said.

He stressed that establishing a permanent fire service base in Hela is vital as the province continues to grow.

“We need proper fire prevention, emergency response, rescue services and protection for our people, public buildings, businesses, schools, hospitals and other properties,” he said.

"As a new province, Hela must keep building strong government services and institutions. Bringing the Fire Service closer to our people will improve our ability to respond quickly to fires, accidents, disasters and other emergencies. We will start in Tari and later expand to the districts and LLGs,” Angu said.

He said this is an important step towards building a safe, prepared and developing Hela Province.

item.title: Government must prioritise resources for frontline border personnel
item.description: The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary’s border commander has called on the National and Provincial Governments to urgently provide resources and support to border agencies, warning that PNG’s sovereignty is at risk without proper border management. Assistant Commissioner of Police border commander Steven Francis issued the statement during the closing of the Paramilitary Training for Border Comm
item.content:encoded:
The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary’s border commander has called on the National and Provincial Governments to urgently provide resources and support to border agencies, warning that PNG’s sovereignty is at risk without proper border management.

Assistant Commissioner of Police border commander Steven Francis issued the statement during the closing of the Paramilitary Training for Border Command personnel at the Forward Operating Base in Vanimo, West Sepik.

ACP Francis said border agencies stationed in key locations including Wutung and the proposed border post at Kiunga require immediate funding, logistics and institutional support.

"Our frontline border personnel are serving in challenging and isolated conditions. They should not be expected to protect the nation without the right tools, technology, facilities and political support," he said.

"Government leaders must move beyond statements of concern and provide practical and timely assistance."

He said while significant attention is given to internal law and order, border security and border management must not be neglected.

ACP Francis highlighted that PNG shares a land border with Indonesia and a maritime boundary with Australia, making border security vital to national sovereignty, economic security and international responsibilities.

He warned that the increasing movement of illicit goods is a clear sign that stronger measures are needed.

"Transnational crime does not respect national boundaries. There are growing concerns regarding the smuggling of fauna and flora, gold and other high-value commodities. Such activities deprive Papua New Guinea of revenue, damage the environment and contribute to organised crime," ACP Francis said.

The border commander stressed that border security is not the responsibility of police alone.

He said police, defence, immigration, customs, quarantine, fisheries and forestry must be properly staffed, trained, equipped and supported to work together.

ACP Francis listed key priorities the government must address including proper funding for border agencies and border provinces, modern border-management systems and smart surveillance technologies ,improved infrastructure at Wutung Kiunga and other border locations,reliable transport,communications and maritime patrol capability, Regular training and welfare support for frontline

ACP Francis concluded that investing in border security is not an unnecessary expense.

"Investing in border security is an investment in national sovereignty, public safety, economic protection and the future security of Papua New Guinea. A country that cannot properly monitor and control its borders remains vulnerable to illegal entry, organised crime, weapons trafficking and the loss of national resources," ACP Francis said

He urged the national and provincial governments and all responsible agencies to act now and make border security a sustained national priority.

item.title: ‘Selfish and greedy’: President slams perpetrators of Panguna mine attack
item.description: Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama has condemned the violent assault on personnel and destruction of equipment at the Lloyds Metals camp in Panguna over the weekend. The attack, which occurred in the early hours of Sunday morning at the Panguna Mine pit in Central Bougainville, involved criminals armed with high-powered weapons who vandalized and torched millions of Kina worth of machinery and
item.content:encoded:
Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama has condemned the violent assault on personnel and destruction of equipment at the Lloyds Metals camp in Panguna over the weekend.

The attack, which occurred in the early hours of Sunday morning at the Panguna Mine pit in Central Bougainville, involved criminals armed with high-powered weapons who vandalized and torched millions of Kina worth of machinery and property.

One suspect was killed and another wounded during a shootout with responding police officers.

Member for North Nasioi, Johns Potabu, clarified that the incident was purely criminal and not linked to local landowners. He stated that the perpetrators—individuals profiting personally from illegal operations in the area—executed the attack to derail Lloyds Panguna Metals and Energy Limited from continuing development at the site.

President Toroama emphasized that the Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) and its people would not be intimidated by factions attempting to derail the mine’s redevelopment.

"While the majority of Bougainvilleans look forward to this development, certain elements have chosen to undermine the authority of the government and the collective efforts of our people," Toroama said.

"The actions of these individuals are selfish and serve only their own greedy intent. They do not have the best interests of our government or our people at heart. This type of behavior has no place in Bougainville and will not be tolerated."

Toroama confirmed that the Bougainville Police Service, supported by a coordinated community effort, is actively working to apprehend all remaining suspects.

"I want to reassure our people that this morning's incident does not weaken us; it only strengthens our resolve. We will take all necessary steps to enforce the government’s mandate to reopen the Panguna Mine," Toroama added.

"Let me be very clear: this government is of the people and by the people. We will not cower to terroristic acts of violence designed to cause disunity and distract us from our agenda of creating a socio-politically and economically viable Bougainville."

item.title: Voluntary gun surrender gains momentum under “Make Hela Safe Again” initiative
item.description: ​The ongoing law and order intervention in Hela Province, operating under the banner "Make Hela Safe Again," reached another milestone over the weekend as more high-powered guns were voluntarily surrendered. ​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed that at 3:51 PM on Saturday, 12 September, local youths voluntarily stepped forward to surrender two additional high-powered firearms—an AK-47 assault r
item.content:encoded:
​The ongoing law and order intervention in Hela Province, operating under the banner "Make Hela Safe Again," reached another milestone over the weekend as more high-powered guns were voluntarily surrendered.

​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed that at 3:51 PM on Saturday, 12 September, local youths voluntarily stepped forward to surrender two additional high-powered firearms—an AK-47 assault rifle and an SR8 tactical rifle.

​Governor Undialu commended their resolve to reject violence in favor of community peace and personal growth.

​"I extend my sincere thanks to these young people for making the courageous choice to lay down their arms," Governor Undialu said "My administration guarantees that they will not be left behind.

“We are actively linking these individuals into education pathways, technical skills training, and Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) support so they can rebuild their lives as productive, contributing members of society." Undialu said.

​Governor Undialu emphasized that the "Make Hela Safe Again" initiative extends far beyond the physical collection of weapons.

​"This program is fundamentally about transforming lives, protecting families, and opening real pathways for our youth," he noted. "We are asking our people to choose peace over violence, education over destruction, and legitimate enterprise over crime to secure a prosperous future for our children." He said.

​The latest handover follows another voluntary surrender earlier in the week, when a young man personally delivered an M16 A2 service rifle to the Governor’s residence. Governor Undialu shared the young man's words: “This gun has destroyed my life and destroyed our communities. I want to change. I want to become a better person.”

​"It takes immense courage to admit that and walk away from conflict. I have personally pledged to assist him in returning to school and starting an SME. This is the positive transformation we want to see across every district in Hela," he said.

​Governor Undialu renewed his call to remaining armed youths across the province, urging them to follow this example by putting down their weapons, embracing education, and joining the growing wave of peace building throughout Hela.

item.title: Resilient sweet potato variety shields Hela farmers from El Niño
item.description: For most rural families across Papua New Guinea, sweet potato [kaukau] is essential to daily life. It serves as both a primary staple food and a reliable source of household income through local markets. However, as severe El Niño drought conditions sweep through the nation, traditional kaukau crops are increasingly failing.
item.content:encoded:
For most rural families across Papua New Guinea, sweet potato [kaukau] is essential to daily life. It serves as both a primary staple food and a reliable source of household income through local markets.

However, as severe El Niño drought conditions sweep through the nation, traditional kaukau crops are increasingly failing.

​In response, weather-resistant kaukau varieties are proving to be a vital lifeline.

In the Hayapuga community of Tari-Pori District, Hela Province, local farmers are now reaping the rewards of climate-resilient agriculture. Despite the ongoing drought, community leader Henry Kumapugo reports that their fields have yielded a successful harvest.

​Kumapugo, who has long advocated for community members to return to their land and focus on farming, distributed drought-resistant kaukau vines to local households. The hardier crops survived the prolonged dry spell, securing both food supplies and income for participating families.

​Beyond subsistence, the initiative is driving local commerce. Mr. Kumapugo is leading the community in supplying bulk kaukau to Wonderland Agri Stock in Hides to support its commercial piggery operations.

​“Communities in Hela Province that planted weather-resistant sweet potato varieties are enjoying the benefits and continuing to earn money by supplying Wonderland Agri Stock,” Kumapugo said.

“With new varieties and clean-propagation methods developed to withstand extreme climate shifts, many households have been sustained through this drought.” Kumapugo said.

​The community thanked the DDA for allocating K500,000 to subsidize the purchase price of kaukau, raising the payout to farmers from 80 toea to K1.30 per kilogram.

item.title: SP Brewery backs Goroka Show with K20,000

item.content:encoded:
South Pacific Brewery has reaffirmed its longstanding commitment to the Goroka Show with a sponsorship of K20,000, continuing its support for one of Papua New Guinea’s most iconic cultural events.

The Goroka Show represents seven decades of cultural preservation, celebration, and shared heritage. Originally established to promote peace and unity among tribes, the event has grown into a symbol of national identity and cultural pride.

Presenting the cheque, SP Brewery representative, John Tole, expressed the company’s delight in supporting the annual event.

“We are proud of our longstanding partnership with the Goroka Show Committee and are delighted to once again support the biggest cultural show in the Highlands region,” Tole said.

“SP Brewery remains committed to supporting initiatives that promote culture and unity within communities. We are pleased to contribute to showcasing the diverse traditions of the Eastern Highlands Province, as well as those of neighboring regions,” he added.

On behalf of the Goroka Show Committee, Chairlady Keryn Hargreaves thanked SP Brewery for its continued partnership and support.

“SP Brewery is one of our longest-standing partners, and their ongoing support plays a vital role in sustaining cultural events like the Goroka Show. We sincerely appreciate their commitment and recognition of the work carried out by the committee. We look forward to delivering another successful show this year,” she said.

SP Brewery will be present at the festival from the 18th-20th of September 2026, with a booth promoting its Join the Generation of Change campaign. The campaign reinforces the company’s commitment to responsible consumption and promoting respect within communities.

Festival attendees aged 18+ are invited to visit the booth to learn more, engage with the SP Brewery staff on ground, and make a pledge to be part of the generation of change.

item.title: Madang police gearing up for 51st Independence celebrations
item.description: Madang police are prepared for the province's two- day 51st Independence celebrations from 15th to 16th September. Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim said policing arrangements have been activated across all six districts to ensure the celebrations are conducted in a safe, peaceful, and well- managed manner.
item.content:encoded:
Madang police are prepared for the province's two- day 51st Independence celebrations from 15th to 16th September.

Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim said policing arrangements have been activated across all six districts to ensure the celebrations are conducted in a safe, peaceful, and well- managed manner.

The PPC has instructed all police personnel to remain highly vigilant before, during, and after all official programs and community activities connected to the independence festivities.

He also said that members of the public can expect increased police presence in key areas, including main event venues, town centres, transport routes, and other locations where big crowds are expected.

Superintendent Baim emphasized, "Police will strictly deal with anyone who attempts to disrupt the celebrations or undermines public safety."

He warned that those who intend to cause trouble will face consequences under the law.

“We will not tolerate anyone trying to disrupt the celebrations. You will be severely dealt with according to law,” Baim said.

He further reminded the people of Madang that Independence is not only about celebration but also about meaningful reflection and renewed commitment.

"This important national milestone should encourage a positive transformation in attitudes and behavior—moving from negative practices to constructive actions that strengthen both communities and the nation.

“Independence is a time for a shift in our mindsets—change attitudes from bad to good. Think of what little things we can do for the development of the province and the country,” the PPC said.

He added that citizens must also understand that development requires support from everyone—not only institutions and leaders.

Baim urged residents to play their part by maintaining a good mindset, respecting one another, and avoiding actions that can create disorder during the Independence period.

“If you don’t want to be part of development for Madang, you better pack up and go home. There could be better things for you to do at home than just staying in urban areas without a good mind frame,” he said.

In addition to maintaining peace and order, Madang police is also reminding small craft owners and boat operators to take seriously the advice and warnings issued by the national weather service during periods of adverse weather.

People are urged to avoid unnecessary travel and to follow official guidance for safety.

PPC Baim stressed that police rescue capacity can be limited during dangerous weather conditions. He therefore urged all concerned parties to prioritize safety over schedules and journeys.

“All small craft owners must take heed of the warning from the National Weather Service. Stop travelling in bad weather conditions.

"Police can’t go into bad weather to rescue you. We are human beings just like you, with very limited resources—so be very mindful of that,” said PPC Baim.

He further encouraged cooperation among community members, including friends and families who may urge others to travel despite warnings.

According to PPC Baim, the safest decision during storms or hazardous weather is to stay ashore until conditions improve.

Baim is calling on all residents, event participants, and visitors to celebrate responsibly.

The command also urged people to observe lawful conduct at all times, avoid disturbances, and respect public peace.

"I also urge communities to refrain from harmful behaviour such as vandalism, fighting, and any acts that could threaten lives and properties.

“People of Madang must celebrate in colours without any interference,” Baim said.

Meanwhile, the special Independence police operation will be launched on Monday.

item.title: Infant amongst survivors of Madang boating incident
item.description: An infant and an eleven-year-old boy were amongst survivors of a boating incident between Raikos and Madang on Friday, police confirmed. Provincial Police Commander for Madang, Superintendent Robert Baim revealed that a motorised dinghy carrying 18 people, including the operator, departed Saidor Station at 7am yesterday and was three hours into the trip when they encountered rough seas at Tabalip
item.content:encoded:
An infant and an eleven-year-old boy were amongst survivors of a boating incident between Raikos and Madang on Friday, police confirmed.

Provincial Police Commander for Madang, Superintendent Robert Baim revealed that a motorised dinghy carrying 18 people, including the operator, departed Saidor Station at 7am yesterday and was three hours into the trip when they encountered rough seas at Tabalip Point, 18 nautical miles south of Madang Town.

All 18 persons were thrown into the sea when the boat capsized.

"They were adrift for about five years or until 3pm when a passing vessel that was travelling to Raikos spotted them and rescued 10 of them. They were immediately taken to the provincial hospital for medical assessment.

"A second search and rescue operation was subsequently conducted, during which a further five survivors were located and rescued, brining the total number of survivors rescued or located to 15 persons out of the original 18 persons on board," PPC Baim said.

According to medical officers at Modilon Hospital, the survivors who were assessed were generally in good condition, with no serious injuries or medical conditions reported.

Some survivors experienced general fatigue and tiredness and were medically cleared.

Superintendent Baim added that three persons remain unaccounted for.

They include 1 male adult, 1 adult female; and another 11-year-old boy.

The three missing persons are believed to have entered the water wearing yellow life jackets and reportedly swam in the direction of the Bilbil area.

Police have notified Ileg Police Outpost and requested assistance in alerting coastal communities in the Bugati area and the wider Astrolabe Bay region to remain vigilant and immediately report any sighting or information concerning the missing persons.

Superintendent Baim said the incident highlights the serious dangers posed by unsafe marine travel, particularly when vessels are operated beyond their safe capacity or when operators fail to properly assess sea and weather conditions.

“The safety of passengers and crew must remain the highest priority whenever travelling by sea.

"Overloading a dinghy or small craft can make the vessel unstable and significantly increase the risk of an accident, particularly in rough weather or challenging sea conditions,” Baim added.

Baim, meanwhile; has also directed Water Police to begin fully enforcing the Small Crafts Act and its regulations, warning that operators who disregard marine safety requirements will face the full force of the law.

He said continued incidents are concerning because awareness programs have been repeatedly conducted amongst coastal communities and marine operators.

“Despite repeated awareness programs, we continue to see incidences that can be avoided if operators and passengers strictly comply with safety requirements. Everyone using small crafts must take responsibility for their own safety and the safety of others,” he stated.

Dinghy operators and skippers are reminded to,

Passengers are also encouraged to speak up if they believe a vessel is dangerously overloaded or being operated in an unsafe manner.

Superintendent Baim warned that persons who disobey the Small Crafts Act and its regulations may face enforcement action, including arrest and legal proceedings where applicable.

“Skippers have a responsibility to operate their vessels safely and within their approved passenger capacity. Carrying more passengers than a vessel can safely accommodate puts lives at unnecessary risk,” he said.

The Madang Provincial Police Command is also urging coastal communities in the Saidor, Bugati, Bilbil and wider Astrolabe Bay areas to remain alert and immediately notify Police, maritime responders or other relevant authorities if they see or receive information about the three missing persons.

He said police will continue working with relevant authorities, maritime responders, and coastal communities to support search and rescue efforts, promote responsible marine transport, and strengthen compliance with marine safety requirements throughout the province.

PPC Baim's message to the people of Madang is to protect lives, comply with the law, and travel safely.
